title: The Industrial Revolution: How Machines Remade the World

questions.question: The Industrial Revolution began around 1760 in:
questions.rationale: Britain combined coal, colonial capital, agricultural surplus labour, and textile demand — the unique starting stack.

questions.question: Which chronological order of textile inventions is correct?
options: Power loom → spinning jenny → flying shuttle
Flying shuttle → spinning jenny → water frame → power loom
Spinning jenny → flying shuttle → cotton gin
Water frame → spinning mule → flying shuttle
questions.rationale: Kay's flying shuttle (1733) speeded weaving; Hargreaves' jenny (1764) and Arkwright's water frame (1769) caught spinning up; Cartwright's power loom (1785) mechanised weaving.

questions.question: James Watt's crucial improvement to the steam engine (patented 1769) was:
questions.rationale: Watt's separate condenser saved the cylinder's heat, making steam power economical everywhere — not just at coal mines like Newcomen's engine.

questions.question: The Stockton–Darlington railway (1825) and the Rocket (1829) are associated with:
questions.rationale: The Stephensons proved steam traction on public railways; Trevithick built the first steam locomotive (1804), and Brunel engineered broad-gauge lines and great steamships.

questions.question: The Luddites (1811–16) were:
options: Early trade unionists seeking higher wages
Machine-breakers protesting job losses in the mills
questions.rationale: Handicraft workers (stocking-frames in Nottingham) smashed the machinery pauperising them; the government made machine-breaking a capital offence.

questions.question: The Factory Act of 1833 in Britain:
options: Banned children under 9 from textile mills and limited child working hours, with inspectors to enforce it
questions.rationale: The 1833 Act set age limits and hours for children in textiles and — crucially — appointed factory inspectors; unions were legalised in 1824–25 and the Corn Laws repealed in 1846.

questions.question: Which country industrialised fastest outside Europe and North America, in a single generation after 1868?
questions.rationale: Meiji Japan's state-led modernisation — missions abroad, model factories, universal schooling — went from feudal to industrial power by the 1890s.

questions.question: In colonial India, early industrialisation was marked by:
options: Cotton mills in Bombay and jute mills in Bengal, with railways from 1853
Steel mills founded by the British East India Company
questions.rationale: Cowasjee Davar's Bombay cotton mill (1851) and Bengal jute mills pioneered modern industry; the Bombay–Thane line (1853) began the railways; Tata Steel followed at Jamshedpur (1907).

questions.question: The Bessemer converter (1856) revolutionised production of:
questions.rationale: Bessemer's process blew air through molten pig iron to burn off carbon, making inexpensive steel — the material of rails, ships, and skyscrapers.

questions.question: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'drain theory' responded to:
options: Colonial extraction of India's wealth to Britain — wealth from industry's peripheries
questions.rationale: Naoroji (and R.C. Dutt) quantified how India's exports without equivalent returns drained wealth to Britain — the economic critique that fed early nationalism and linked industrialisation to empire.
